kicker: Project Maya, read from the source

scenes.headline: How a 321B model runs on two old GPUs
scenes.sub: Project Maya: experts in VRAM, in RAM and on the SSD.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tiffin! Let's see how two old datacenter cards run a giant model.

scenes.text: Each token uses 8 of 288 experts per layer, so the busiest live on the GPU, the next in RAM, the rest on the SSD.
scenes.mark: the busiest live on the GPU
scenes.say: Each token needs eight experts per layer. Busy ones stay on the card, the next in memory, the rest on disk.

steps.say: The router picks eight experts. Most already sit in that layer's slots.
A miss in pinned memory is pulled across the bus into a spare slot, and stays.
One in neither is read from the drive while the card waits.
Between tokens, each layer's least used expert moves down, freeing a spare.

scenes.title: One expert, three prices
scenes.note: one 7.11 MB expert on the launch machine
scenes.say: From card memory, an expert takes microseconds. Over the bus, half a millisecond. From the drive, three.

steps.say: The layers are split across two cards, so each would idle half the time.
So the draft layer guesses the next token, and the first card starts early.
A right guess keeps both busy. A wrong one is rerun.

scenes.title: Why a long chat stays fast

steps.label: The indexer scores every pool
steps.say: Each sparse layer scores every pool of four past tokens. That part grows, cheaply.

steps.label: Attention reads only the top pools
steps.say: Attention reads only the top two thousand positions, however long the chat.

steps.label: A radix select picks them
steps.note: the first version ranked every pool against every other
steps.say: The engine's first ranking grew with the square of the context. A radix select fixed it.

scenes.title: The fix, in their own chart

steps.say: Their chart: grey, the old ranking, climbing with context.
Purple is the radix select, near a tenth of a millisecond.

scenes.label: of expert lookups must hit VRAM for 40 tokens a second
scenes.note: 28.0 tok/s over five chat topics, in the engine's own log
scenes.say: Forty tokens a second needs about ninety seven percent of lookups on the card. Over five chats, their log says twenty eight.

scenes.text: Speed is set by how many lookups leave the GPU, so more RAM beats more GPU.
scenes.say: Speed is lookups leaving the card. Here, more memory is the cheapest way up.

recap: Busy experts on the GPU, the rest below
A draft token keeps both cards busy
Sparse attention keeps long chats fast
scenes.say: Busy experts on the card. A draft keeping both cards working. Cheap attention.
